title: This BORING Business Makes $3M/yr From My Laptop
promo_conflict: The title says $3M/yr, while the supplied transcript only claims the business does “well into the seven figures,” so the exact $3M figure is not substantiated there. Zenbooker receives a positive endorsement; no sponsorship disclosure appears in the supplied transcript.

stated_problem.quote: Somehow, someone booked a sofa removal on my website, but they were hours away.
stated_problem.speaker: Tim Richard

idea.name: Remote nationwide junk removal
idea.one_liner: Take online junk pickup bookings across multiple cities, send jobs to local subcontractors, and keep the difference between the customer price and contractor payout.
idea.customer: US households, with a commercial side as the business grows.
idea.offer: Customers select junk items, book and pay online; local subcontractors collect the items.
idea.revenue_model: Charge customers upfront and pay subcontractors per job, retaining the margin.

key_quotes.quote: If people can book online on my website, pay with an upfront price, and I send the job out to someone in that area who already picks up junk, I could do this all over the country.
And really, to get into a new town, all I had to do was expand my website to rank in these new towns, and then find contractors, subcontractors to be able to [music] pick up the items in those towns.
So, if I'm paying them, you know, $75 to pick up a three-seat sofa, I'd be trying to get $150 from the customer.
So, from the booking, from the selecting of the items to the payment to the sending it out to contractors, it allows me to just run it all from my computer.

I would start in my town, I would get a Google business listing in my town, build a website, and, you know, post on my local Facebook community page, stuff like that, to get initial customers in my town right off the bat.

claims.claim: He reports having no employees or trucks and doing none of the jobs himself.
claims.quote: I don't have any employees, I don't have any trucks, I don't do any of the jobs myself

claims.claim: He usually targeted about 50% profit per job.
claims.quote: I usually aimed for about a 50% profit.

claims.claim: For a three-seat sofa, the example contractor payout is $75 and the target customer charge is $150.
claims.quote: So, if I'm paying them, you know, $75 to pick up a three-seat sofa, I'd be trying to get $150 from the customer.

claims.claim: He has a database of over 5,000 subcontractors.
claims.quote: I have a database of over 5,000 subcontractors that I can send jobs out to.

claims.claim: He says he has run the business for 15 years.
claims.quote: I've been running this for 15 years

claims.claim: The business operates in over 40 major cities and ranks in hundreds of cities.
claims.quote: we operate in over 40 major cities nationwide, we rank in hundreds of cities across the country

claims.claim: He says the business does well into seven figures; the transcript does not specify the period or accounting basis.
claims.quote: Today, we do well into the seven figures

claims.claim: He says he does not use paid advertising and relies on organic acquisition.
claims.quote: I really don't do any paid ads, it's all organic.

acquisition_channels.details: Built unique city and item pages and ranked them in organic search.
Suggested posting on a local Facebook community page to get initial customers.
Described word of mouth and Google reputation as helping the business grow.
Used Craigslist and Thumbtack to find subcontractors, not described as customer lead sources.
Called prospective local junk haulers to ask if they would take jobs.

ideas.delivery: Online booking and payment feed job details to area subcontractors through Zenbooker; the subcontractor performs the physical pickup and is paid by the operator.

prices: $75 contractor payout for a three-seat sofa
$150 customer price for a three-seat sofa
platforms: Google My Business / Google Business listing
